titel: Bacteria and temperature: the danger zone
kurz: Bacteria multiply fastest between about 10 and 50 °C. Cold slows them down; thorough heating kills most of them.
bild_im_kopf: Like weeds in spring: in mild weather they grow overnight; in frost and in heat they rest.
was_passiert: In pleasant warmth, bacteria divide every few minutes to hours. The fridge slows them down a lot but does not kill them. Only enough heat makes meat and leftovers safe: food safety authorities recommend at least 70 °C at the core. Cooked food should pass through the warm range quickly, taking at most about two hours to cool.
warum_wichtig: Explains why poultry is cooked through, why leftovers should not sit on the stove for hours and why keeping food warm means keeping it hot.
faustregeln: Heat poultry, minced meat and leftovers to at least 70 °C at the core.
Keep food warm at 65 °C or more, otherwise cool it quickly.
Put leftovers in shallow containers in the fridge within two hours.
Thaw in the fridge, not on the kitchen counter.

stellschrauben.wirkung: the longer in the warm range, the more germs

praxis.text: Always cook chicken through: at least 70 °C at the core for two minutes.
Do not leave cooked rice standing warm for long; cool it quickly.

params.hinweis: Guide values from food safety authorities
